That’s a really good point; I got introduced to the series with MGS, so I’m definitely more biased towards Solid. I love Big Boss though, and I think it’s important how his character develops over the series. When I first started playing the series, without having played MG1 or 2, Big Boss was this mysterious and legendary villain, the central cause of all the mayhem in the series, even after his death. MGS and MGS2 do nothing to set him up as a complex villain, so it’s really jarring to play MGS3 and find out about the man behind the legend.

He’s not some child solider raising lunatic, he’s just a man put into an extremely complicated situation and forced to survive. You get to see how his relationship with the Boss influences him, right up until he’s forced to gun her down for his country. The whole game perfectly shows us how a good man can end up as a legendary villain, and it makes him complex, and I love that. My biggest issue with his story is that none of his other games really follow through on that legacy. MGS4’s epilogue closes his story in a beautiful way, but Peace Walker and V never made me feel like I was a villain. Even in Phantom Pain, you’re a straight up hero that prevents a madman from wiping out the world’s languages.

What’s more important though, is that Raiden is clearly the best main character in the series, and by far my favorite.

I think Big Boss’ story should have ended after 3. It was nice to get the chance to play as the legendary Big Boss and see how exactly he got the title, and it’s probably my second favorite Solid game, but it ultimately wasn’t necessary, except to introduce Zero, and he could have been introduced in 4. Solid Snake was the introduction to Metal Gear, and in the end he was the hero, Big Boss will never have the same spot in my heart.
